chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about a man who stands in prayer and forgets the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha).
He said: 'Let him say: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.' Then let him recite it (Al-Fatiha) as long as he has not yet bowed.
For there is no recitation until he begins it in a loud or quiet voice, for if he bows, it will suffice him, if Allah the Exalted wills.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: It suffices him / It is accepted
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they forget to recite Al-Fatiha during prayer?
ai.summary: In the Shia jurisprudential tradition, this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes that omitting Surah Al-Fatiha is a correctable error rather than a nullifier, provided the substitute recitation occurs before entering *ruku'*. Shaykh al-Tusi utilizes this report to demonstrate the flexibility in obligatory recitations, emphasizing that the essential condition is the commencement of the prayer's verbal components before the physical transition to bowing.
